query: For AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for additively manufactured miniature components, what single intervention could overcome the residual thermal stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions, states the applicable processing window, geometry, and test conditions, identifies supporting prior evidence, and describes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) of as‐printed AlCrFeNiSi miniature components will relieve residual thermal stresses and improve mechanical properties by promoting beneficial phase transitions and dislocation rearrangement.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCrFeNiSi parts fabricated via conventional high‐thermal‐load laser powder bed fusion that exhibit high residual thermal stresses, degraded yield strength and ductility, and complex, non‐optimized microstructures.
generation.intervention: Apply a deep cryogenic treatment post-printing by immersing the as-built components in liquid nitrogen (approximately -196 °C) for an extended period (e.g., 12 hours) followed by controlled warming to room temperature.
generation.conditions: Components with miniature features (1–10 mm scale) manufactured under typical L-PBF conditions; testing performed at room temperature using standardized tensile tests and X-ray diffraction (XRD) for residual stress analysis.
generation.structural_mediator: Recrystallized grain refinement accompanied by dislocation reordering and potential formation of nano-scale precipitates that serve to relax internal stresses.
generation.mechanism: The cryogenic treatment induces a phase adjustment and reorganization of dislocations that release stored thermal stresses, while also encouraging beneficial microstructural changes which enhance yield strength and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to untreated components, DCT-treated parts will exhibit statistically lower residual stress levels (as measured by XRD), higher yield and ultimate tensile strengths, and improved elongation.
generation.baseline: Conventional high-thermal-input L-PBF components that, due to rapid solidification, retain high levels of residual thermal stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and a less favorable microstructural state.
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of DCT may be confined to miniature-scale components and could vary with subtle differences in processing parameters and alloy-specific phase responses; quantitative improvements remain to be precisely determined.
generation.uncertainty: While the proposed mechanism is based on analogous benefits observed in other alloy systems undergoing DCT, the exact magnitude of mechanical improvement and stress reduction for AlCrFeNiSi requires further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two identical sets of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components using conventional L-PBF processing. Subject one set to the proposed deep cryogenic treatment (immersion in liquid nitrogen for 12 hours, followed by controlled warming) while leaving the other set untreated. Perform X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis to quantify residual stress and conduct standardized tensile tests to measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation.
measurements: Residual stress via XRD (peak shifts, strain analysis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the DCT-treated samples do not show statistically significant reductions in residual stress and improvements in tensile properties relative to the untreated control group, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

Material-agnostic machine learning approach enables high relative density in powder bed fusion products

Abstract: This study introduces a method that is applicable across various powder materials to predict process conditions that yield a product with a relative density greater than 98% by laser powder bed fusion. We develop an XGBoost model using a dataset comprising material properties of powder and process conditions, and its output, relative density, undergoes a transformation using a sigmoid function to increase accuracy. We deeply examine the relationships between input features and the target value using Shapley additive explanations. Experimental validation with stainless steel 316 L, AlSi10Mg, and Fe60Co15Ni15Cr10 medium entropy alloy powders verifies the method’s reproducibility and transferability. This research contributes to laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing by offering a universally applicable strategy to optimize process conditions. Synergistic Strength–Ductility Improvement in an Additively Manufactured Body-Centered Cubic HfNbTaTiZr High-Entropy Alloy via Deep Cryogenic Treatment

Abstract: AbstractHfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy has wide application prospects as a biomedical material, and the use of laser additive manufacturing can solve the forming problems faced by the alloy. In view of the characteristics of the one-time forming of additive manufacturing methods, it is necessary to develop non-mechanical processing modification methods. In this paper, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) is first applied to the modification of a HEA with BCC structure, then the post-processing method of DCT is combined with laser melting deposition (LMD) technology to successfully realize the coordinated improvement of forming and strength–ductility synergistic improvement in lightweight Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy. The final tensile strength of the alloy after DCT treatment is 25% higher than that of the as-cast alloy and 11% higher than that of the as-deposited alloy, and the elongation is increased by 48% and 10%, respectively. In addition, DCT also achieves induced phase transition without additional deformation.Keywords: laser
